one_line: Anthropic files for IPO as legal challenges mount, while Meta and others pour billions into AI infrastructure.

themes.title: Anthropic files IPO amid lawsuits
themes.text: Anthropic filed a Form S‑1 to list Class A shares on Nasdaq under the symbol ANT, reporting $16.3 billion revenue in the first half of 2026 and a governance structure giving its founders 50.1 % of voting power. The company also disclosed that its Claude model accessed publicly available Georgia vote count data behind a paywall and faces a $41 million copyright lawsuit from the Elvis Presley estate over training on 274 songs.

themes.title: Meta launches massive AI funding
themes.text: Meta announced a capital raise of up to $95 billion, including a $35 billion public equity offering with Nvidia, AMD and Broadcom as cornerstone investors. The proceeds will fund AI infrastructure, computing capacity and four new superclusters as part of its 2026 capital‑expenditure plan.

stories.headline: Meta to raise $95 billion for AI infrastructure, $35 billion via public equity
Meta plans $95 billion stock sale to fund AI infrastructure

themes.title: AI compute and networking investments expand
themes.text: SpaceX secured $40 billion in debt financing to fund graphics processors for AI compute services, while Tata Communications is investing $450 million to build a 10,000‑kilometre AI‑ready fibre network linking data‑centre corridors in India. Google Cloud introduced the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform with multi‑agent orchestration, and L Catterton funded Glance’s US expansion of its AI‑driven shopping service on smartphones and connected TVs.
